### Investment Memo: GPC — October 30, 2026

**Verdict**: HOLD (event-driven INITIATE at 1.0% for special-situations sleeves) | Conviction: Medium
**Price Target**: $130 (+5% from current $123.52); SOTP bull case $145–155; downside case $106
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months (hard-dated catalyst: Q1 2027 separation)

---

**Investment Thesis**

GPC is a deteriorating-but-honest, thin-margin replacement-parts distributor whose equity story has collapsed into a single event: the Q1 2027 tax-free separation into Global Automotive (NAPA, ~$15B) and Global Industrial (Motion, ~$9B), with a reported ~$10B O'Reilly bid for NAPA as a live second catalyst. The core operations are in structural, not cyclical, decline — ROIC 20.3% → 9.6% in three years, FCF −63% since 2022, operating margin 7.6% → 5.0%, and a dividend funded at 134% of FCF with debt. At ~16x adjusted 2026 EPS and 0.70x sales, the market already prices most of the decay, and clean forensics (Beneish −2.60, four years of negative accruals, expanding adjusted gross margin) rule out a fraud short. This is a catalyst trade with a balanced risk/reward, not a value or income investment.

---

**Key Findings by Domain**

- **Macro & Sector**: Macro unfavourable — 10Y at 5.15% has compressed the equity risk premium to ~105bp and the 3.4% dividend now sits 175bp *below* the risk-free rate, killing the income bid; energy-led CPI (3.72% headline vs 2.57% core) squeezes the auto customer. Lone macro positive: industrial production +2.2% feeding Motion (+6% in Q3'26). Sector neutral — defensive, non-discretionary demand and an aging fleet (~12.8 yrs), but channel-wide gross-margin compression and late-mature 3–5% growth. GPC is a margin **and** growth laggard (+3.5% vs +6.9% peer median; 5.0% vs 16.7% op margin), partly structural (jobber-owned NAPA model).
- **Geopolitical & Legal**: MEDIUM risk. All rule-of-law jurisdictions — no EM/confiscation profile. Real exposures: realised tariff costs (China/Mexico/Canada), a war-adjacent underperforming European business (~16% of sales), an unsettled **asbestos tail** (part of the $1.1B FY25 charges), and the **§355 tax-free spin qualification** as the gating legal item — a taxable spin would be company-changing.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Value**: Narrow moat, narrowing. Blended intrinsic value **~$120 (range $95–135)** — current price sits *above* the midpoint, i.e., no margin of safety. SOTP at peer multiples gives ~$129–145. ROIC collapse is the classic moat-erosion signature; goodwill/intangibles of ~$5.0B = 106% of book equity after a $1.0B impairment that itself confirms past M&A overpayment.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Growth**: Fails any growth mandate (Rule of 40 ≈ 5; ~3% organic). The growth case is purely event-driven: Form 10 disclosures (H2 2026), separation (Q1 2027), and the ORLY NAPA bid. Motion's automation/reshoring exposure is the only genuine frontier pocket. Consensus EPS path $7.75 → $9.02 (~8% CAGR) is credible only on an adjusted basis.
- **Quantitative Signals**: Composite 41/100 — neutral. Normalized forward P/E 16.0x / EV/EBITDA 12.7x are the only usable multiples (trailing figures are impairment artifacts). Momentum reversing (−8.7% last month); quality decaying; **R² vs SPY = 0.03** — 97% idiosyncratic, so it neither hedges nor tracks a cyclical book. Alpha statistically insignificant.
- **Financial Risk**: MODERATE, trending High into the split. Adjusted net leverage ~3.0x (net debt down $1.74B in 9 months to $6.06B), BBB-/negative; interest coverage 7.3x. But quick ratio 0.54, FCF yield 2.45%, and a **−15% revenue decline is the covenant break-point** — a 5%-margin distributor has ~7x profit gearing to revenue. Refinancing legacy low-coupon paper at 5%+ rates adds ~$150–200M of hidden after-tax earnings drag.
- **Non-Financial Risk**: MODERATE (upper end). The dominant flag: **Chair/CEO Stengel is negotiating the debt/pension/overhead allocation while committed to run Motion — the counterparty is his own future employer.** New external CEO at the remaining auto business; three guidance trims in four quarters; zero insider buying through a 40% drawdown. Clean enforcement/litigation record otherwise.
- **ESG**: Average, governance-laggard. ISS Governance decile 8 / Board decile 9; CEO pay +67% to $12.9M into a margin-compression year; 331:1 pay ratio; combined Chair/CEO. Environmentally low-risk but bottom-quartile disclosure (no GHG inventory, no CDP) → screened out of ESG mandates. Not a thesis driver; a quantifiable multiple drag.
- **Alternative Data**: BEARISH into the Feb 16, 2027 print. Category search interest −17% YoY with no Q4 seasonal build; corporate-name attention at 12-month lows (the event-driven bid has unwound); and **Q4 consensus ($1.74) sits ~6% above the guidance-implied midpoint (~$1.64)** — the bar is set high, not low. Industrial demand is the one unverified pillar.
- **Short / Contrarian View**: **Reject the short.** Honest accounting, expanding adjusted gross margin, non-discretionary demand, 0.68 beta, and a ~1:2.7 risk/reward *against* the short ($107 downside vs $167 upside). The bear case is slow-bleed capital-allocation decay, already substantially priced after the −37% Feb–May drawdown.

---

**Bull Case**
- **Double-barrelled catalyst**: Q1 2027 separation (Motion re-rating toward GWW/FAST-type multiples; NAPA pure-play de-conglomerating) plus a reported ~$10B ORLY bid for NAPA; SOTP $145 = ~20% upside before any bid premium.
- **Defensive cash flows + idiosyncratic profile**: non-discretionary repair demand, 0.48–0.68 beta, 0.17 correlation to SPY — genuine diversification with embedded optionality.
- **Self-help is working at the margin**: three consecutive adjusted EPS beats, Q3 gross margin +70bp, net debt cut $1.74B in nine months, and Elliott on the register enforcing accountability.

**Bear Case**
- **Structural quality decay**: ROIC below WACC, inverted operating leverage (SG&A +8.2% vs revenue +3.5%), FCF −63% in three years, and a 69-year dividend streak now debt-funded (134% of FCF).
- **Near-term air pocket**: alt data points to a Q4 miss against a consensus set ~6% above the guidance midpoint; estimate-cut risk into February.
- **Separation tail risks**: taxable-spin failure, second impairment at Motion, adverse debt allocation, or dis-synergies >$100M — any one converts the catalyst into a permanent value impairment on a levered (BBB-) balance sheet.

**Key Risks**
1. §355 tax-free qualification failure or spin delay past mid-2027 (binary, uninsurable).
2. Governance conflict producing a debt/pension allocation that handicaps one stub — watch >$5B on Motion.
3. 10Y above ~5.3% compressing the multiple to ~14x (~$105) even with earnings intact.
4. FY26 FCF <$350M with the dividend held — second consecutive debt-funded payout.
5. Tariff escalation on Mexico/Canada auto parts (USMCA breakdown).

**Portfolio Construction Note**
Initiate **1.0% (hard cap 3.0%)** as an event-driven/special-situations position — explicitly *not* as a defensive or income holding (the yield no longer clears the 10Y, and realised vol is 36%). Fund from any existing AZO/ORLY/HD/LKQ sleeve. Ladder: 1.0% now, +1.0% only after the Feb 16 print *and* Form 10 shows Motion standalone EBITDA ≥12% with separation costs <$75M; +0.75% at ≤$108. No adds above $132; trim one-third at $140; bank the position at $152–158. Hard stop: weekly close below $105. Exit immediately on any thesis-invalidation trigger (taxable spin, spin delay, second Motion impairment, FY26 adj. EPS ≤$7.50, net leverage >4.25x, or current ratio <1.0). The **debt allocation disclosed at separation is the single most informative number in the file** — re-underwrite the entire position on it.

---

*Significant disagreement flagged: Value (IV $120, no margin of safety) vs Growth (SOTP $145) — resolved by treating GPC as a catalyst trade, not a value investment. Data gaps: agency credit ratings/CDS unverified, full 10-K and DEF 14A text unavailable, insider buy/sell direction and Motion segment-level financials unconfirmed.*

# GPC (Genuine Parts Company) — Portfolio Construction Recommendation
**As of Oct 30, 2026 · Price $123.52 (Oct 20 close) · Mkt cap ~$17.0B · EV ~$25.0B · 3.4% yield**

---

## 1. Agent Conviction Summary

| # | Agent | View | Conviction | Key Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Value Researcher** | Bearish/Neutral | **High** | Blended IV ~$120 (range $95–135). Price **above** the value-based midpoint → **no margin of safety**. ROIC 20.3%→9.6% in 3 yrs; FCF −63% since 2022; dividend 134% of FCF. |
| 2 | **Fin Risk Analyst** | Negative | **High** | Net debt $6.06B (improved from $7.80B); adjusted leverage ~3.0x, BBB-/negative. Quick ratio 0.54, current ratio 1.22. FCF payout 134%. Fails a −15% revenue stress test. |
| 3 | **Short Analyst** | **No edge / reject short** | **High** | Beneish −2.60, 4 yrs negative accruals, adjusted GM *expanding*. Risk/reward **1:2.7 against the short**. "Deteriorating but honest" — not a fraud. |
| 4 | **Non-Fin Risk** | Negative on governance | **Med-High** | ⚑ **CEO Stengel is negotiating the split and will run Motion — the counterparty is his own future employer.** Second guidance trim; 331:1 pay ratio; no insider buying through a 40% drawdown. |
| 5 | **Macro Researcher** | Unfavourable | **Med-High** | 10Y **5.15%**, 30Y 5.37%. EPS yield 6.2% − 10Y = **~105bp ERP**, historically thin. 3.4% dividend now **175bp *below* the 10Y** — the income bid is gone. Industrial production +2.2% is the lone positive. |
| 6 | **Sector Researcher** | Neutral | Medium | Margin **and** growth laggard (3.5% vs +6.9% peer median; 5.0% vs 16.7% op margin). 16x adj. EPS already discounts it. Q1'27 split is the only credible catalyst. |
| 7 | **Growth Researcher** | Hold | Medium | Fails growth mandate (Rule of 40 = 5.2, ~3% organic). **SOTP support ~$145**; live ORLY ~$10B NAPA bid = double-barrelled catalyst. Upgrade at Form 10 or a confirmed/raised bid. |
| 8 | **Alt Data Analyst** | **Bearish** | Medium | Category search **−17% YoY**, no Q4 seasonal build; **Q4 consensus ($1.74) ~6% above the guidance midpoint**. Retail/event bid fully unwound (corporate search at 12-mo low). Overrides its own +0.83 sentiment print as stale. |
| 9 | **Quant Analyst** | Neutral | Medium | Composite **41/100**. **R² vs SPY = 0.03** — 97% idiosyncratic. 12-1 momentum +5.7% but 1-mo −8.7% (reversal). Rejects the tool's +19% revision "upgrade" as a period mismatch. |
| 10 | **Geo Legal** | Medium risk | Medium | No EM/confiscation/sanctions profile. Realised tariff cost channel; **asbestos tail**; **§355 tax-free spin is the gating risk**. |
| 11 | **ESG Analyst** | Neutral / slight negative | Medium | ISS Governance **decile 8, Board decile 9**. CEO pay +67% into a margin-compression year. Bottom-quartile environmental disclosure → screened out of ESG mandates. |
| — | *Coverage note* | — | — | 11 specialist reports received. No dedicated dividend/income or technical-timing report; both would be additive given FCF coverage and the Feb 16, 2027 print. |

---

## 2. Consensus Assessment: **SPLIT** — but with high-conviction agreement *around* the edges

**Where agents genuinely agree (high confidence):**
- **Do not short.** Short, Quant, Value and Sector all independently land on "not a fraud, bad news largely priced."
- **Quality has deteriorated structurally, not cyclically.** Value, Fin Risk, Short, Quant and ESG converge on ROIC decay (20.3%→9.6%), inverted operating leverage, and a dividend no longer cash-covered.
- **The Q1 2027 separation is the whole thesis.** Growth, Sector, Non-Fin Risk, Macro and ESG all identify it as the dominant catalyst — and all five flag it as the dominant *risk*.

**Where they conflict (the actual debate):**

| Debate | Bulls | Bears | My resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cheap or value trap? | 16x adj. EPS, 0.70x sales, SOTP $145 | Price > IV midpoint $120; 2.45% FCF yield vs 5.15% 10Y | **Both true.** Cheap vs. peers, not cheap vs. its own cash flows or the risk-free rate. This is a **catalyst trade, not a value investment.** |
| Near-term direction | Separation + bid optionality | Alt data bearish into Feb 16; consensus 6% above guide midpoint | **Bears win the next 3–4 months.** Bulls win the 12–18 month horizon *if* the spin executes. |
| Governance | Board responded to Elliott | CEO conflict + ISS decile 8 | **Conflict is real and unmitigated.** It is a sizing input, not a pass/fail. |

**Fraud/forensic overlay:** the Short Analyst's forensic toolkit (Beneish, accruals, adjusted gross margin) **fails to confirm** the bear case. Per my conflict-resolution rule, the fraud flag is absent — so the bear case reduces to a leverage/cash-flow/capital-allocation case, which is a *sizing* problem, not an *exclusion* problem.

---

## 3. Position Sizing Recommendation: **1.0% of portfolio to initiate; 3.0% hard cap**

**Scenario-weighted edge (my own construction):**

| Scenario | Prob. | Price | Return | Contribution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Separation closes cleanly; Motion re-rates; NAPA bid firm | 25% | $158 | +28% | +7.0% |
| Separation closes; modest re-rating, dis-synergies absorb upside | 40% | $131 | +6% | +2.4% |
| Q4 miss → estimate cut; spin delayed past mid-2027 | 25% | $106 | −14% | −3.5% |
| Taxable spin / second impairment / covenant event | 10% | $82 | −34% | −3.4% |
| **Expected return** | | | | **+2.5%** |

**Kelly check:** E = +2.5%, σ ≈ 20% → full Kelly ≈ 0.6x leverage; frankly the edge is too thin to size aggressively. **Quarter-Kelly ≈ 5–6%.** Then apply explicit haircuts for the risk flags that Kelly cannot see:

- **−50% for separation execution + tax-free qualification risk** (binary, uninsurable, non-diversifiable within the name)
- **−50% for balance-sheet fragility + governance conflict** (CEO negotiating against his own future employer → adverse allocation of debt/pension is a live, unpriceable risk)

**→ 1.0–1.5% initial. I recommend 1.0%.**

This is deliberately below my own framework's "medium conviction / elevated risk = 1–3%" lower bound, because **four** independent risk flags (leverage, FCF coverage, governance conflict, spin-tax) all sit on the same event. Correlated risks of that type do not get a mid-range size.

---

## 4. Portfolio Fit Analysis

**Sector concentration — acceptable.** Nominally tagged Consumer Cyclical, but GPC is economically a replacement-parts distributor. If the book already holds AZO/ORLY/HD/LKQ, **fund this from that sleeve** rather than adding fresh cyclical exposure — GPC is the cheapest expression of the same end-demand with a company-specific catalyst attached.

**Correlation — genuinely attractive (tool-verified, 252d):**

| Pair | Correlation |
|---|---|
| GPC–SPY | **0.17** |
| GPC–GWW | **0.24** |
| GPC–AZO / ORLY | 0.38 / 0.39 |
| GPC–FAST | 0.40 |
| GPC–LKQ | **0.58** (highest — do **not** pair) |

**R² vs SPY = 0.03.** This is a near-pure idiosyncratic bet — it adds return potential without importing market beta. That is the single strongest portfolio-level argument for the position.

**Factor exposure — the tension.** Beta is genuinely low (0.48 tool / 0.68 profile) but **realised volatility is 36.4%** with a −37.5% max drawdown and a **Sharpe of 0.12 (and −0.094 on the Sharpe/Sortino tool)**. So:
- ✅ *Reduces* portfolio market beta — defensive in a drawdown
- ❌ *Increases* portfolio volatility and adds a "quality-laggard / deep-value" tilt
- ❌ Adds to an **event-driven / special-situations** bucket — cap total bucket exposure at ~10%.

**Book it as event-driven, not as a defensive core holding.** Sizing it as a low-beta staples substitute would misprice its risk.

---

## 5. Entry Strategy: **Laddered scale-in — 3 tranches, not all at once**

Current $123.52 sits **above** value-IV ($120) and mid-way between the July low ($108.65) and Aug high ($138.81). Recent analyst actions are split: Goldman cut to $122 and UBS at $122 *below* spot, while Truist raised to $131 and D.A. Davidson/Raymond James sit at $165–170. Alt data is bearish into Feb 16, 2027.

| Tranche | Size | Trigger | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T1 — now** | **1.0%** | At market, or on a pullback to $118–121 | Buy the catalyst optionality; do not pay up for it |
| **T2 — Feb 16, 2027** | +1.0% | Post-Q4 print **and** Form 10 discloses Motion standalone EBITDA ≥12% and separation costs <$75M | Resolves the two biggest unknowns simultaneously |
| **T3 — on weakness** | +0.75% | Price ≤ $108 (≈ value-IV low end; higher margin of safety) with no thesis-invalidation trigger | Adds at a genuine discount |
| **Do not add** | — | Above **$132** | Risk/reward inverts; 90% of blended IV ($120–145 → ~$132) reached |

**Explicit rule: no adds between now and the Feb 16, 2027 print.** The Alt Data Analyst's Q4 downside call and the 6% above-midpoint consensus bar are too specific to ignore, and T2 is designed to capture the information, not to pre-empt it.

---

## 6. Risk Management Rules

**Hard stop (price):** weekly close below **$105** (−15%). That sits just under the July 21 intraday low of $108.65 and brackets the short analyst's $107 downside case. Cost at 1.0% weight: **−15bp of portfolio.** Do not use a tighter stop — 36% annualised vol will whipsaw it.

**Thesis invalidation (exit on any one — these override price):**
1. **Separation slips past mid-2027**, or the Form 10 misses its SEC review timeline.
2. **Taxable spin** — §355 opinion/IRS ruling fails or is qualified. Binary, company-changing.
3. **FY2026 adjusted EPS ≤ $7.50** (low end) or Q4 2026 GAAP EPS < $2.00 — confirms consensus ~$7.74 is unattainable.
4. **FY2026 FCF < $350M with the dividend held** — second consecutive debt-funded payout.
5. **Second goodwill impairment**, specifically at Motion (of the $4.95B, 106% of book equity).
6. **Net debt/EBITDA > 4.25x**, or **current ratio < 1.0** (currently 1.22).
7. **Debt allocation places >$5B on the ~$1.1B-EBITDA Motion stub** (>4.5x leverage on the lower-quality asset) — the specific governance-conflict outcome to watch.
8. **Annualised interest expense > $250M** (10Y at 5.15% makes refinancing the legacy low-coupon paper materially dearer than the 2.0% current effective rate implies).

**Trim triggers:**
- **$132** (+7%) — 90% of blended IV ($120–145). *Stop adding, hold.*
- **$140** (+13%) — trim **one-third**. The de-rating has happened; banking some catalyst premium is correct.
- **$152–$158** (+23–28%) — trim to a **runt position** or exit. At that level you are paid for the decision, not the execution.
- **On separation completion:** exit the pair rather than hold either stub, *unless* the Motion stub trades below 11x standalone EBITDA at the time of distribution.

**Position-level governance escalation (from Non-Fin Risk):** before T2, request from the Lead Independent Director written confirmation of (a) whether CEO Stengel recused from the debt/pension/overhead allocation and (b) whether his separation comp is tied to Motion's standalone valuation rather than total shareholder value. **If the answer is adverse, cancel T2 and reduce T1 to 0.5%.**

---

## 7. Final Portfolio Action: **INITIATE — 1.0% of portfolio**

**Rationale in one line:** A cheap, low-correlation, genuinely defensive-demand distributor with a hard-dated Q1 2027 re-rating catalyst and a live strategic bid — held to a deliberately small size because the catalyst's success sits in the hands of a board whose CEO is negotiating on behalf of his own future employer, on a balance sheet that cannot absorb a miss.

**What this is:** an **event-driven / special-situation** position, sized on catalyst optionality — **not** a value or income position (3.4% yield now sits 175bp *below* the 10Y, and FCF covers the dividend only 0.75x).

**What this is not:** a pass. The Short Analyst's own numbers ($107 downside / $167 upside = 1:2.7 against the short), the clean forensics, and the 0.17 correlation to SPY all say the risk is worth 100bp of capital. It is not worth 400bp.

**Re-underwrite at:** Feb 16, 2027 (Q4/FY26 + first 2027 guide), the H2 2026 Form 10 and investor days, and any §355 tax opinion disclosure — whichever comes first. The **debt allocation at separation** is the single most informative number in this entire file.

# GPC — Sector Brief: Auto & Industrial Parts Distribution

**Note on classification:** FMP tags GPC as "Consumer Cyclical / Auto-Parts," but GPC is economically a **two-headed replacement-parts distributor**: ~$15B automotive aftermarket (NAPA, DIFM-weighted) and ~$9B industrial/MRO (Motion Industries). The screen's default Consumer Cyclical peer list (AMZN, TSLA, HD, MCD) is useless here, so I built a purpose-built peer set of the four listed auto aftermarket distributors/retailers (AZO, ORLY, LKQ, AAP) plus the three large industrial distributors (GWW, FAST) that are Motion's direct competitors. As of the Q3'26 report (Oct 20, 2026), GPC is pre-separation — the auto and industrial businesses become two public companies in **Q1 2027**.

## 1. Sector Overview

The relevant sector is **replacement-parts distribution** — a structurally defensive, mature, working-capital-intensive channel business that earns money on inventory density, branch/store density and local delivery, not on proprietary product. Both sub-sectors are large and highly fragmented: the US automotive aftermarket is roughly $430B across all channels (~3.8% CAGR), with the four traditional distributors (AutoZone, O'Reilly, NAPA/GPC, Advance) holding the professional/DIFM share while the US MRO market grows at only ~2% nominal and is split among thousands of players (GWW $17.9B, GPC industrial ~$9B, FAST $8.2B, plus Applied, Motion rivals, Amazon Business). Sector growth has decelerated sharply from the 2022–23 inflation/M&A boom (GPC +17% in FY22, GWW +17%) to a **3–5% organic world in 2025–26**, and the sector is now in a late-mature, slow-growth phase where **relative margin execution, not top line, determines share-price outcomes.**

## 2. Key Tailwinds

- **Aging vehicle fleet + deferred maintenance:** average US vehicle age is at record highs (~12.8 years), and DIFM (professional repair) volume is the structural growth engine — the same tailwind lifting ORLY to its 33rd consecutive positive comp year. Replacement demand is non-discretionary and largely recession-insulated.
- **Industrial demand inflecting off a soft 2024–25 base:** GPC's industrial segment grew **+6% to $2.4B** in Q3'26, FAST printed **+8.7%** FY25 revenue growth with its strongest monthly daily-sales growth since early 2023, and reshoring/data-centre/automation/infrastructure capex is driving MRO and power-transmission demand. Automation/robotics is an explicit growth vector for Motion.
- **Structural consolidation and pricing:** tariffs are a **net positive for large distributors** — they carry the balance sheet and supplier relationships to pass through cost (and to hold inventory ahead of price increases), while smaller jobbers cannot. Sector surveys show ~half of small aftermarket players with a negative outlook on tariffs vs. larger players gaining share.

## 3. Key Headwinds

- **Gross-margin compression across the channel:** GPC's gross margin has fallen from 36.3% (FY24) to 34.6% (FY25); LKQ from 40.8% (FY22) to 38.0% (FY25); AAP from 46.3% (FY22) to 43.4%. Auto parts inflation has reversed into deflation/mix drag, and tariff cost recovery is lagging.
- **Freight, fuel and wage inflation against soft consumer demand:** Q3'26 commentary explicitly cites "elevated fuel costs and freight inflation" and "cautious consumer conditions" suppressing retail auto and deferrable maintenance. GPC's SG&A grew faster than sales (Q3'26 SG&A $1.94B on +4.2% revenue), so gross-margin gains were fully absorbed — op margin fell to 5.2% from 5.3%.
- **Secular channel threat from e-commerce and OE/dealer parts:** Amazon Business, direct-ship manufacturer programmes and private-label penetration erode the distributor's traditional markup; industrial MRO is the most exposed, which is why GWW/FAST are spending heavily on vending/digital (a capex and SG&A arms race GPC must fund).

## 4. Peer Comparison Table

| Company | Rev (FY, $B) | Rev growth (latest FY) | Gross margin | Operating margin | Mkt cap ($B) | P/Sales |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **GPC** | **24.30** | **+3.5%** | **34.6%** | **5.0%** | **17.0** | **0.70x** |
| AZO | 20.34 | +7.4% | 52.3% | 18.3% | 51.6 | 2.54x |
| ORLY | 17.78 | +6.4% | 51.6% | 19.5% | 72.8 | 4.09x |
| GWW | 17.94 | +4.5% | 39.1% | 15.0% | 62.9 | 3.51x |
| FAST | 8.20 | +8.7% | 45.0% | 20.2% | 59.3 | 7.23x |
| LKQ | 13.92 | −3.1% | 38.0% | 7.8% | 5.45 | 0.39x |
| AAP | 8.60 | −5.4% | 43.4% | 1.9% | n/a | n/a |
| **Peer median (ex-GPC)** | — | **+6.9%** | **44.2%** | **16.7%** | — | — |

*Multi-year trend (GPC):* revenue growth +14.1% / +17.1% / +4.5% / +1.7% / +3.5% (FY21–FY25, 8.0% CAGR, M&A-inflated); gross margin 35.2% → 35.0% → 35.9% → 36.3% → **34.6%**; operating margin 6.2% → 7.3% → 7.6% → 6.1% → **5.0%**. FY25 included a Q4 restructuring/impairment charge (net loss of −$609M on the quarter). Latest quarter (Q3'26): revenue $6.52B (+4.2% YoY), gross margin 38.1% vs 37.4%, operating margin 5.2% vs 5.3%, diluted EPS $1.62 ($2.07 adjusted). FY26 adjusted EPS guidance narrowed to **$7.50–$7.75** → ~16x at $123.52, with a ~3.3% dividend yield.

## 5. Target Company's Competitive Position: **Average**

**Rationale.** GPC has genuine scale — it is #1/#2 in North American automotive aftermarket (NAPA, ~6,000 stores, DIFM-heavy, plus a large company-owned store base in Europe/Australasia) and #2 in North American industrial distribution (Motion, ~$9B). Those are durable, high-barrier positions: local inventory depth, delivery fleet density and 65,000 employees are not replicable by a new entrant.

But it is a **clear margin laggard and a growth laggard**:

- **Growth:** +3.5% vs. peer median +6.9%, and every one of AZO (+7.4%), ORLY (+6.4%), FAST (+8.7%), GWW (+4.5%) beat it. GPC is losing relative share in a growing market.
- **Margins:** 34.6% gross / 5.0% operating vs. 44.2% / 16.7% medians. Part of the gap is structural, not managerial — NAPA's network is heavily **independent (jobber-owned)** stores, so GPC books wholesale revenue at low margin, whereas AZO and ORLY consolidate ~100% company-operated stores at 51–52% gross margin. GPC's true comparison is the **industrial distribution trio**, where the gap is still stark: GWW 15.0%, FAST 20.2% vs. GPC 5.0% and LKQ 7.8%. Motion should be a high-teens-margin asset and isn't visible in the consolidated number.
- **Momentum is negative:** gross margin down 170bp and op margin down 110bp in FY25, with Q3'26 earnings missing consensus and guidance trimmed. That is a share-losing, cost-inflation-losing pattern.
- **Valuation already discounts it:** 0.70x sales vs. 2.5–7.2x for GWW/FAST/AZO/ORLY, and ~16x adjusted EPS. Only LKQ trades cheaper.
